message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the 2003 Mr. Basketball America and the 2004 Naismith High School Player of the Year.

He was selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers and quickly became the face of the franchise. LeBron has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), the Miami Heat (2010–2014), and the Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). LeBron has also been selected to the NBA All‑Star Game 19 times (as of 2023) and has earned numerous All‑NBA and All‑Defensive Team honors.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I’m‑a‑STEM” school in Akron in 2018. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment, and has appeared in several movies and TV series.

LeBron’s impact extends beyond statistics; he is celebrated for his leadership, versatility, and longevity, consistently performing at an elite level into his late 30s. He remains a central figure in discussions about the greatest basketball players of all time.
